Cisco Routing and Switching Learning Hub

Welcome to the Cisco Routing and Switching learning hub by IT Education Nepal (ITEN). This repository offers free, practical, beginner-friendly resources to help students, career-transition learners, NOC trainees, and aspiring network engineers build real-world networking skills from the ground up.

Instead of relying on passive theory or pre-built lab files, every guide in this hub follows a hands-on engineering approach: build the network yourself, verify how it works, troubleshoot real faults using command-line evidence, and document your results like a working professional.

Available Book: Junior Network Engineer Assignments (Volume 1)

Title: Junior Network Engineer Assignments: Zero-to-Networking Practical Lab Guide (Volume 1: Foundations to Switching)

This book is a complete, step-by-step practical lab guide written for absolute beginners and junior network engineers preparing for real operational roles and the Cisco CCNA certification track. You do not need any pre-configured .pkt or .pcapng files to complete the assignments. Build every topology from scratch in Cisco Packet Tracer.

What You Will Learn and Build

Module 0: Day Zero and Getting Started
Set up your lab workspace, install Cisco Packet Tracer, inspect your own computer's network stack, build your first two-PC switched network, and get comfortable with the Cisco IOS command-line interface (CLI).

Module 1: Network Foundations
Build small-office Ethernet LANs, choose the right cabling, configure Cisco IOS device identity and banners, manage running and startup configurations, observe ARP and MAC learning in action, interpret interface states, and troubleshoot end-to-end paths with ping and traceroute.

Module 2: IP Addressing and the Subnetting Mastery Track
Configure IPv4 hosts and default gateways, master binary-to-decimal conversion and fast block-size subnetting without a calculator, design Variable-Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) addressing plans, configure IPv6 link-local and SLAAC addressing, and isolate dual-stack network faults.

Module 3: Switching and Network Access
Configure switch management SVIs, CDP and LLDP neighbor discovery, VLAN segmentation, voice and IoT edge ports, 802.1Q trunking, Router-on-a-Stick subinterfaces, Multilayer Switch SVI routing, Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree, PortFast and BPDU Guard protection, LACP EtherChannel link bundling, and real-world NOC switching tickets.

How to Start

Open the Volume 1 Markdown Book and review the introductory setup checklist in Module 0.

Create a local working folder on your computer (Junior_Network_Engineer_Labs/Volume-1/) to save your .pkt topologies, CLI verification outputs, and troubleshooting notes.

Work through each lab in sequence, complete the Mixed Reviews at the end of each module, and use the built-in Appendices for CLI error lookup, command reference, and self-check validation.
